provenance: Telephone call, 2026-09-13, Larry's son asking the four cold van questions from the head of the interview guide, exactly as written and with nothing else said or shown first, and typing Larry's answers as he spoke them. This answer is to: "What was the name or number of the outfit that ran the van?" Raw capture: research/interviews/breakfast-questions.md, annotated in place under each question.
text: I think it belong to 18th Avaiation because it was over in theior stuff and we had been using one of their offices. We used the offices for our radios. It was a pretty big office area. On that street was the EM Club which was called the playboy club which was a big club. It was a big company. They had their own paratroopers, there own maintenance department. I don't know what happened when we left there of what happened to them. They may have been absorbed into the 1st Cavalry. Our Unit was so small, I don't think we even had a medic. We had a cook, I got seperate rations because I was gone at The Mountain but I could have eatin in the mess hall if I was there.
researchNotes: Last of the four, asked cold: no unit, number or "AOD" supplied. He did not say AOD, 118th, or detachment. THE PROBE DID NOT PRODUCE THE PRINTED DESIGNATION, and it must never be written up as confirming it. What he gave is "18th Aviation" for the third time, after 2026-08-23 and VN-0011 on 2026-09-12. This time he says plainly what he means by it: the organisation whose ground the van stood on and whose offices his section used for its radios. It is not his own unit: "Our Unit was so small, I don't think we even had a medic." 18th Aviation, in his telling, was a big company with its own paratroopers and maintenance department, and an EM Club on that street called "the playboy club". So he describes two organisations: a large host, and his own small unit with a cook and no medic, which he does not name. That fits, without confirming, the finding in research/units/18th-aod-stars-and-stripes-1964.md that two different "18th" organisations existed, a small detachment and a large aviation company. Which one he means by "18th Aviation" is research. Leads, kept out of rendered fields: (a) "the playboy club". "Playboys" was the call sign of a Tan Son Nhut helicopter platoon, and is the leading candidate for the VN-0012 tail emblem (research/magnification/README.md). He supplied the word himself, so it was not primed, but the emblem probe stands: describe no emblem to him. (b) "absorbed into the 1st Cavalry" is a third form of the 1st Cavalry association (ledger #2), here attached to the host company after he left, not to him. (c) Separate rations for the man on the mountain. Keystrokes as typed: "Avaiation", "theior", "of what happened", "eatin", "seperate". HIS SON'S NOTES ON THE CALL, given the same evening in answer to follow-up questions (the typist's observations and readings, not Larry's words): (1) He said "18th" for certain, not "118th". (2) "The playboy club": his son understood it as a nickname for a large EM Club on 18th Aviation's street or area, given for its size, not as a formal name. That weakens, without removing, the call-sign lead in (a) above. Asked later that evening whether it is the same EM Club Larry has put 50 yards from his hooch (VN-0030 to VN-0034), his son could say only what Larry said: a big club on 18th Aviation's street. Whether that is the hooch club, and so whether his hooch was on that street, is open. (3) "They had their own paratroopers, there own maintenance department": "they" is 18th Aviation, the host, not Larry's own unit. (4) Most of what he added about 18th Aviation was about how large it was. He also said "C Street" in connection with them. It was not typed during the call. His son first gave it hedged, then confirmed later that evening that Larry definitely said "C Street", though neither of them knew what he meant by it. Treat it as Larry's word, reported by his son (paraphrase-strength). He said it himself, so asking what he meant does not prime him: "You mentioned C Street — what was that?" Offer no guess at its meaning. (5) The rations were not explained on this call. On a different day, in a conversation not recorded, Larry described having a different access to food, from a building that was not the mess hall. Whether cash was involved was never asked and never said. His son at first recorded "not cash in place of meals", then corrected it the same evening: that was his own assumption, drawn from Larry not mentioning cash. Open.
